chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who borrows white dirhams by number and repays black ones by weight, while he knows that they are heavier than what he took, and he is content to give him the excess.
He said: There is no harm in it so long as there is no condition in it; and even if he were to gift all of it to him, it would be valid.

key_terms.أَثْقَلُ: heavier in weight than the original amount
key_terms.شَرْطٌ: a stipulated condition in the loan agreement
key_terms.وَزْنًا: by weight, rather than by count
key_terms.ٱلدَّرَاهِمَ: dirhams, the monetary units under discussion

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan with more than what was borrowed if the extra amount was not stipulated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on repayment of a loan with dirhams of greater weight than those originally borrowed. The Imam عليه السلام permits this additional amount when it is given voluntarily and not stipulated as a condition, distinguishing lawful goodwill from usury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4025 - Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who borrows a specified amount of white dirhams and repays them with black dirhams by weight, knowing that they are heavier than what he borrowed, and he willingly gives the extra weight.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it as long as it is not a condition. Even if he gifted him all of it, it would be permissible."
